```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(gatekeepR)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = TRUE)
```

`gatekeepR` turns per-cell marker measurements into reviewable phenotype and
state calls. The same prepared objects and classifier are used by batch code,
the review application, and the locked export. This keeps a reviewed result
replayable after the interactive session has ended.

## The complete workflow

The following code is the smallest end-to-end template. It uses a configuration
and a panel declared as data, then carries the result through correction,
thresholding, classification, state calls, structures, review, and export.

```{r workflow}
cfg <- gk_example_config()
cells <- gk_simulate(n_cells = 300L, seed = 7L)
prep <- gk_prepare(cells, config = cfg, quiet = TRUE)
corrected <- gk_correct(prep, method = "robust_z")
thresholds <- gk_thresholds(prep, cfg, correction = corrected, seed = 7L)
classification <- gk_classify(prep, thresholds, config = cfg, correction = corrected)
states <- gk_state_calls(prep, thresholds, classification, config = cfg)
structures <- gk_structures(classification, prep)
review <- gk_review(classification, states, structures, thresholds, prep)
reviewed <- gk_replay(review)

snapshot <- gk_lock(review, reviewer = "example-reviewer", status = "PENDING")
export_dir <- tempfile("gatekeepR-example-")
gk_export(snapshot, dir = export_dir)
stopifnot(all(gk_verify_export(export_dir,
  expected_review_id = snapshot$review_id_full)$ok))
```

PENDING is deliberate: running an example does not complete scientific review.
Warnings about disabled rules identify unsupported channels in the simulated
panel and are retained as evidence in the export.

`gk_replay()` is the review boundary: it applies the append-only ledgers to
the initial calls and returns the effective reviewed state. `gk_save_review()`
and `gk_load_review()` persist the review package before export when work must
be resumed later.

## Outputs and auditability

The `classification`, `states`, and `structures` objects retain the cell and
image identifiers needed to join results back to source data. A locked export
contains the effective calls, review ledgers, configuration, provenance, and a
manifest. `gk_verify_export()` checks the manifest and replays the exported
decisions, so downstream code can reject incomplete or contradictory exports.

## Optional interfaces

Plots are thin views over the same objects used by batch code:

```{r plots, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
image_id <- prep$cells$image_id[[1L]]
gk_plot_map(reviewed, image_id = image_id)
gk_plot_thresholds(thresholds, image_id = image_id)
gk_plot_overview(reviewed, image_id = image_id)
```

The review app can load a review or an exported result with
`shiny::runApp(gk_app(review = review))` or
`shiny::runApp(gk_app(export = export_dir))`. The app does not create
a separate classification implementation.
